title: Lithostratigraphy of the deep corehole (Clubhouse Crossroads corehole 1) near Charleston, South Carolina
citation: Gohn, G.S., Higgins, B.B., Smith, C.C., and Owens, J.P., 1977, Lithostratigraphy of the deep corehole (Clubhouse Crossroads corehole 1) near Charleston, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 1028-E [p. 59-70], map scale 1:1,040,763.
notes:
The PDF is the whole Professional Paper 1028 volume (chapters A-O), not only chapter E. This packet covers chapter A (Rankin, introduction and discussion) and the start of chapter B (Bollinger, intensity data). Chapter A summarizes results from other chapters (Gohn and others, Hazel and others, Gottfried and others, Ackermann, Campbell, Phillips, Tarr); values here are attributed to chapter A pages. CCC 3 values come from a footnote added after the chapter was written. Chapter B content is mostly macroseismic intensity and building damage; only craterlet ground effects were recorded. Figures 1-5 of chapter B are maps whose text is garbled and were skipped. References: recorded those on South Carolina geology, seismicity and the Coastal Plain from chapter A's list (p. 26-27); skipped general plate-tectonic, seismological and non-SC references. Chapter B text continues in packet-02.

References: recorded those on South Carolina geology, seismicity and the Coastal Plain from chapter A's list (p. 26-27); skipped general plate-tectonic, seismological and non-SC references. Chapter B text continues in packet-02.
Pages 42-80 cover the end of chapter B (Bollinger, intensity attenuation and magnitude), chapter C (Bollinger and Visvanathan, pre-1886 seismicity, archival felt reports) and most of chapter D (Tarr, recent seismicity). These are seismological chapters: intensity tables, felt reports, hypocenter tables and a layered P-wave velocity model (table 2, p. 76) have no fields in the extraction schema and were not recorded. Recorded only structural interpretations (seismic zones, the November 22, 1974 nodal plane, Taber's hypothesized buried fault) and South Carolina references. Chapter D continues into packet-03 (its reference list starts on p. 80). Skipped general seismology references (attenuation, magnitude, California, Europe, eastern Tennessee).
Pages 81-115: end of chapter D references, all of chapter E (Gohn and others, lithostratigraphy of CCC 1, pp. 87-98, the cataloged chapter) and the first part of chapter F (Hazel and others, biostratigraphy, pp. 103-115; continues in packet-04). Each formation has two unit entries: one from chapter E (lithology, thickness, contacts) and one from chapter F (ages, fossils, paleoenvironment). The chapter F summary table (p. 103) gives 6 m for the Pleistocene(?) unit where chapter E gives 5 m (16 ft); only the chapter E value was recorded. Chapter A (packet-01) says CCC 1 was drilled in 1974 and 1975; chapter E says January-March 1975; both recorded on their pages. Texture/mineralogy figures 3-6 and the correlation and transgression charts (figs. 3-4 of chapter F) and sedimentation-rate tables were not transcribed; long species lists of ostracodes, nannofossils and mollusks were summarized only by a few key taxa per formation. References: recorded chapter E's South Carolina references (p. 98); skipped North Carolina, New Jersey, Alabama references and the duplicate Colquhoun and Johnson (1968) already recorded from chapter A.
Pages 81-115: end of chapter D references, all of chapter E (Gohn and others, lithostratigraphy of CCC 1, pp. 87-98, the cataloged chapter) and the first part of chapter F (Hazel and others, biostratigraphy, pp. 103-115; continues in packet-04). Each formation has two unit entries: one from chapter E (lithology, thickness, contacts) and one from chapter F (ages, fossils, paleoenvironment). The chapter F summary table (p. 103) gives 6 m for the Pleistocene(?) unit where chapter E gives 5 m (16 ft); only the chapter E value was recorded. Chapter A (packet-01) says CCC 1 was drilled in 1974 and 1975; chapter E says January-March 1975; both recorded on their pages. Texture/mineralogy figures 3-6 and the correlation and transgression charts (figs. 3-4 of chapter F) and sedimentation-rate tables were not transcribed; long species lists of ostracodes, nannofossils and mollusks were summarized only by a few key taxa per formation. References: recorded chapter E's South Carolina references (p. 98); skipped North Carolina, New Jersey, Alabama references and the duplicate Colquhoun and Johnson (1968) already recorded from chapter A.
Pages 116-141: end of chapter F (Hazel and others: planktic foraminifers, spores and pollen, dinoflagellates, references) and most of chapter G (Gottfried and others, geochemistry of the CCC 1 basalt; continues in packet-05). Long species lists and palynological/dinoflagellate zone correlations with New Jersey and Maryland units were not transcribed. Major-oxide, trace-element and K-Ar tables (tables 1-4) have no schema fields and were not recorded except the K-Ar age interpretation. Several chapter G pages have interleaved columns, so quotes were kept short. References: chapter F list recorded only Sanders (1974), the one South Carolina reference not already recorded from other chapters (Cooke 1936, Pooser 1965 and Swift and Heron 1969 are duplicates); chapter G references follow in packet-05.
Pages 142-177: end of chapter G (geochemistry of CCC 1 basalt, references), chapter H (Sass and Ziagos, heat flow in CCC 1) and first part of chapter I (Popenoe and Zietz, geophysical basement; continues in packet-06). Recorded: South Carolina wells that reached basement from chapter I table 1 (pp. 165-166; Georgia and North Carolina wells skipped), each with basement rock type and basement altitude (meters, negative = below sea level; stored as interval description because it is an altitude, not a depth); basement belts and plutons; geophysically interpreted faults, dikes, arches and basins; the Middendorf heat-flow/ground-water observation. Not recorded: geochemical discrimination diagrams, heat-flow table values, gravity/magnetic anomaly descriptions without named features. Well 12's location is printed '8 km SW of Aiken County, S.C.'. References: only South Carolina items not already recorded (Zietz and others 1976; Ziagos and others 1976); chapter G's reference list is otherwise general geochemistry.
Pages 178-217: end of chapter I (Popenoe and Zietz), chapter J (Phillips, magnetic basement) and chapter K (Long and Champion, Bouguer gravity of the Summerville-Charleston epicentral zone). Content is geophysical interpretation; recorded interpreted structures (dikes, plutons, faults, basins), basement depths and the deep Summerville well. Pages 178-179 have two columns interleaved in the text layer, so quotes there are short fragments. Model parameters (cylinder/sphere radii, density contrasts, gravity gradients) were not recorded. References: South Carolina items from chapter I's list (pp. 180-181) not already recorded from other chapters; chapters J and K references (aeromagnetic map 75-590 already recorded; K continues in packet-07) skipped here.
Pages 218-272: end of chapter K references, chapter L (Ackermann, seismic refraction), chapter M (Talwani, quarry-blast crustal model), chapter N (Campbell, resistivity soundings) and chapter O (Kane, gravity highs and earthquake centers). Mostly geophysical; recorded interpreted structures, unit seismic/electrical properties, a freshwater-saltwater interface estimate and South Carolina references. Not recorded: VES layer table (p. 260), traveltime curve parameters, gravity model densities, chapter O comparisons with other eastern US earthquake areas. Two quotes about the quarries' Santee Limestone lithology (p. 237) could not be matched to the interleaved text layer and were dropped. Chapter N footnote on the second corehole (basalt 774-1,031 m, 257 m thick) duplicates CCC 3 data recorded in packet-01.
Scope: this record is chapter E (Gohn and others) of USGS Professional Paper 1028, PDF pages 83-98 of the whole-volume file. Values read from other chapters' pages were removed from this record.

name.quote: amygdaloidal basalt (K/Ar minimum ages: 94.8±4.2 m.y. and 109±4 m.y.), greater than 42 m (137 ft)

rank.quote: amygdaloidal basalt (K/Ar minimum ages: 94.8±4.2 m.y. and 109±4 m.y.)

age.value: Cretaceous(?); K/Ar ages of 109 ± 4 m.y. (latest Early Cretaceous) and 94.8±4.2 m.y. (earliest Late Cretaceous), considered minimum ages
age.quote: 42 m (137ft) of basalt of Cretaceous(?) age

description.value: at least two distinct flow units; lower flow (7 m recovered) has 1.8 m of fractured, altered basalt overlain by 5.2 m with upward-increasing amygdules; upper flow (34.7 m) has 3 m of fractured basalt below 22.9 m of fresh, dark-gray amygdaloidal basalt, grading up into dark-red weathered basalt (4.2 m) and red-, yellow-, and white-mottled clay (4.6 m) with relict amygdaloidal texture
description.quote: The distribution of weathered, amygdaloidal, and massive basalts within the core indicates at least two distinct flow units.

name.quote: The Cape Fear Formation overlies the basalt and contains unconsolidated interbedded clay and sand.

rank.quote: The Cape Fear Formation overlies the basalt
rank.note: rank taken from the unit name

age.quote: Cape Fear Formation, Upper Cretaceous, 59 m (194 ft)

thickness.quote: Cape Fear Formation, Upper Cretaceous, 59 m (194 ft)

lithology.quote: contains unconsolidated interbedded clay and sand

description.value: lower 13 m (42 ft) primarily red or brown clay and less common feldspathic sand with a basal unit of muddy conglomeratic sand; middle part (24 m, 80 ft) thinly interbedded gray-olive silty clay and light-greenish-gray fine-grained sand; upper 22 m (72 ft) knobby reddish-brown to yellowish-gray, noncalcareous, micaceous clay
description.quote: The lower 13 m ( 42 ft) is composed primarily of red or brown clay and less common feldspathic sand and has a basal unit of muddy conglomeratic sand.

contacts.value: base (750 m, 2,462 ft) drawn between an upper conglomeratic muddy sand and the top of the basalt; Cape Fear-Middendorf boundary at 691 m (2,268 ft), at the base of the lowest 0.3 m (1 ft) or thicker feldspathic sand in an interbedded sand-clay sequence
contacts.quote: The base of the Cape Fear Formation (750 m, 2,462 ft) is drawn between an upper conglomeratic muddy sand and the top of the basalt.

depositional_environment.value: unfossiliferous reddish clay and coarse feldspathic sand continental; fossiliferous thinly interbedded sand and dark clay marginal marine
depositional_environment.quote: Unfossiliferous reddish clay and coarse-grained feldspathic sand in the Cape Fear and Middendorf Formations are assigned to the continental environment.

rank.quote: The Middendorf Formation is a thick sequence

description.value: clay pale red or reddish brown or red and gray green mottled, noncalcareous, micaceous; sand poorly sorted, feldspathic, noncalcareous, fine to coarse grained; arranged in 1- to 5-m-thick (3-15-ft) fining-upward cycles
description.quote: The clay, silt, sand, and conglomeratic sand are arranged in 1- to 5-m-thick (3-15-ft) fining-upward cycles.

contacts.value: Middendorf-Black Creek contact placed at 567 m (1,860 ft) on the most pronounced lithologic change; an unconformity of considerable temporal magnitude is present

depositional_environment.quote: and mottled clay deposited in continental environments
